claims.text: The initial eutectic high-entropy alloy has dual-phase lamellar colonies.
The lamellar colonies contain numerous internal boundaries vulnerable to microcrack initiation.
A minute Nb addition can produce coherent nanoscale precipitates at internal lamellar boundaries after suitable heat treatment.
A minute Ti addition can produce coherent nanoscale precipitates at internal lamellar boundaries after suitable heat treatment.
Coherent nanoscale interfacial precipitates provide precipitation strengthening.
The interfacial precipitates deflect or arrest microcrack propagation.
Microcrack deflection or arrest by the precipitates improves room-temperature tensile ductility.
Nb- or Ti-doped and heat-treated samples will have higher yield strength than the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
Nb- or Ti-doped and heat-treated samples will have greater plastic strain at failure than the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
Simultaneous strength and ductility improvements depend on the precipitates remaining nanoscale.
Simultaneous strength and ductility improvements depend on maintaining precipitate coherency.
Excessive precipitate coarsening will negate the proposed improvements.
Loss of precipitate coherency will negate the proposed improvements.
The magnitude of improvement may depend on the specific alloy composition.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that the benefit is conditional on producing nanoscale coherent precipitates, but the falsification rule treats precipitate coarsening or loss of coherency as falsification. Failure to realize the specified mediator places a sample outside the stated boundary conditions and therefore does not, by itself, refute the conditional mechanism.
